title: Whole-Body Dexterity
abstract: Current humanoid dexterous manipulation remains largely confined to end-effectors and simple grasps, falling short of humans' ability to engage the entire body by bracing and sliding bulky objects against the arms and torso. We introduce Whole-Body Dexterity (WBD), a general framework that uses the robot's body and appendages as contact surfaces to grasp and manipulate objects. Our sim-to-real pipeline first generates a dataset of feasible whole-body grasps, then trains reinforcement-learning experts on a general any-to-any repositioning objective by sampling initial and goal grasps from the dataset, and distills these experts into a single policy that uses proprioception and object geometry. We show that the distilled policy transfers zero-shot to a real Unitree G1, where it repositions a basketball and a cardboard box to regions around the torso and completes a long-horizon task that stows a box under one arm, carries it from a shelf to a table, and places it. The controller operates interactively, steered by coarse motion references from a human teleoperator. Across real-world whole-body manipulation tasks, the distilled controller completes 90% of trials, compared with 18% for direct retargeting and 4% for a generalist whole-body controller.

title: Infinite hidden Markov models for cylindrical data
abstract: We propose an infinite hidden Markov model for cylindrical time series with von Mises-Gamma emissions. Posterior inference is performed using a beam sampler combining conjugate updates and approximate sampling schemes. Simulation studies and two real data applications demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed methodology.

title: Towards Uniform Meaning Representation for Brazilian Portuguese: Building a First UMR-Annotated Dataset
abstract: This paper presents the first Brazilian Portuguese dataset annotated for Uniform Meaning Representation (UMR). It contains 96 sentences from the Brazilian Portuguese portion of the Parallel Universal Dependencies treebank, parallel to existing UMR annotations in English, Czech, and Italian. The sentences were parsed with PortParser, revised in Arborator-Grew, converted from CoNLL-U into preliminary sentence-level UMR graphs, and manually revised in PENMAN format. The results show that CoNLL-U is a useful starting point, but semantic graph construction requires manual interpretation and language-specific lexical resources. The dataset expands multilingual UMR coverage and supports future Portuguese semantic annotation.

title: TinySQL: A 125M-Parameter Text-to-SQL Model Built and Pretrained From Scratch on 4.5B Tokens
abstract: We describe TinySQL-125M, a decoder-only language model for text-to-SQL in which every component of the model path is written from scratch: a byte-level BPE tokenizer, the transformer itself (grouped-query attention, rotary embeddings, SwiGLU, RMSNorm), the optimizer, the training loop, the data pipeline, a grammar-constrained decoder and the evaluation harness. The model is pretrained for about 46 hours on a single NVIDIA L4 GPU on 4.5B tokens of educational web text and SQL code, then fine-tuned on WikiSQL. To make the result interpretable, we fine-tune four public models of similar size (GPT-2 124M, Pythia-160M, SmolLM2-135M and SmolLM2-360M) with an identical recipe, sweep the learning rate for every model, average over three seeds, train our architecture without pretraining as a control, and report confidence intervals and paired significance tests throughout. On the WikiSQL test set, TinySQL reaches 77.95 ± 0.18% execution accuracy with greedy decoding and 80.39 ± 0.20% with schema- and value-constrained decoding (official evaluator: 78.03% and 80.50%). This is about one point below GPT-2 and 17 points above Pythia-160M, which was pretrained on 67× more tokens; SmolLM2-135M, pretrained on 2T tokens (about 440× more), is 4.6 points ahead. Pretraining accounts for 41 points of accuracy. Constrained decoding never turned one of our model's correct answers into a wrong one in any paired comparison we ran. Small-scale ablations show that rotary embeddings and tied embeddings matter far more than grouped-query attention or an SQL-heavy pretraining mix, and a hand audit suggests that most remaining aggregation errors are label errors in WikiSQL. Code, results and tests: https://github.com/aditya0929/tinysql

title: Blind pairwise evaluation materials for dictionary-free spelling normalization in a rule-based Uzbek–English MT system (KKT)
abstract: Materials for the final blind pairwise evaluation of the dictionary-free spelling normalization layer (IMLO-2, KKT_IMLO_A) in the rule-based Uzbek–English machine translation system KKT. The archive allows the numbers in Table 5 of the accompanying paper, Cohen's κ and Gwet's AC1 to be recomputed. All files are byte-identical copies from the project repository. System state. Evaluation date 2026-10-08; production build 2026.10.08-49 (code commit 31f5252); dictionary database md5 9d3adf8d. Pool: development set E2119 (2,119 sentences, not a test set); 60 of the 174 sentences whose translation changed under normalization were randomly sampled. Judges. GPT-6 Luna (OpenAI, ChatGPT Temporary Chat) and claude-opus-5-5 (Anthropic, Claude Code). Each judge received two orders of the same 60 pairs (positions swapped, items reshuffled), each order in a separate chat/session. Files. Item files (kor_paket_gpt_1.csv, kor_paket_gpt_2.csv); the unblinding key (kor_kalit.json, with SHA-256 committed before any judgment was collected); raw judge outputs (kor_paket_*_natija.csv); the judge prompt (kor_korsatma_60.md) and pre-registered decoding/acceptance rule (kor_qoida.md); the decoding script (kor_dekod.py, Python 3 standard library) with its output (kor_hukm.json) and manual reason–choice consistency classification (kor_sabab_tasnif.json); and a discarded first run (discarded_run1/), excluded before decoding for design deviations and reported as supplementary only. The README is in Uzbek. Reproduction. Running kor_dekod.py regenerates kor_hukm.json byte-identically. From the 3×3 GPT×Claude agreement matrix in kor_hukm.json, κ = 0.27 and AC1 = 0.68 are reproduced. Agreed pairs: 40 better : 3 tie : 1 worse; the acceptance criterion is met. Integrity: MANIFEST.sha256.

title: ЦИФРОВОЙ ТЕКСТ-АНАЛИЗ ЭЛЕКТРОННЫХ АМБУЛАТОРНЫХ ЗАПИСЕЙ В КЛИНИКО-ЭПИДЕМИОЛОГИЧЕСКОЙ ХАРАКТЕРИСТИКЕ СИНДРОМА ЗАДЕРЖКИ ПСИХОРЕЧЕВОГО РАЗВИТИЯ: ВОЗМОЖНОСТИ И ОГРАНИЧЕНИЯ ЦИФРОВОЙ МЕДИЦИНЫ
abstract: Оценить возможности и ограничения цифрового текст-анализа неструктурированных электронных амбулаторных записей невролога для клинико-эпидемиологической характеристики синдрома задержки психоречевого развития (ЗПРР) у детей. Материалы и методы. Ретроспективно проанализирован массив из 3143 электронных амбулаторных записей одной специализированной неврологической клиники за период с марта 2024 по июль 2026 г. Методом автоматизированного поиска по ключевым терминологическим паттернам в свободном тексте поля «Диагноз» отобраны записи с указанием ЗПРР; выполнены деидентификация, дедупликация повторных визитов (запись-связывание по фамилии, имени и году рождения в отсутствие единого идентификатора пациента) и частотный текст-анализ сопутствующих диагностических терминов. Результаты. Выявлено 69 визитов у 60 уникальных пациентов с ЗПРР (2,2% от общего массива записей); медианный возраст 6 лет (диапазон 2–22 года), соотношение мальчики : девочки ≈ 2,3 : 1. В структуре сопутствующих диагнозов доминировали маркеры хронической герпесвирусной/цитомегаловирусной/Эпштейн-Барр-инфекции (86,7% пациентов), снижение порога судорожной готовности по ЭЭГ (50,0%), гиперактивность (26,7%), последствия перинатальной энцефалопатии (16,7%), детский церебральный паралич (11,7%). У 11,7% пациентов зафиксированы повторные визиты, потребовавшие алгоритма связывания записей. В части записей выявлены структурные аномалии текста (несогласованное форматирование, опечатки в демографических полях), ограничивающие точность автоматизированного извлечения данных. Заключение. Цифровой текст-анализ свободнотекстовых амбулаторных записей позволяет быстро и без создания отдельного регистра получить содержательную клинико-эпидемиологическую характеристику редкого педиатрического синдрома, однако его точность существенно ограничена качеством и структурированностью первичной документации, отсутствием уникального идентификатора пациента и одноцентровым характером выборки.

title: Adaptive Switching Between Self-Supervision and Inter-Model Collaborative Supervision in Self-and-Inter Models: A General Framework for Autonomous Learning and Cross-Model Coordination
abstract: Self-supervision enables a model to generate learning signals from its own observations, internal representations, predictions, experiences, or computational processes. Inter-model collaborative supervision, in contrast, allows multiple models to exchange information and provide complementary learning signals to one another. Although both paradigms offer valuable learning capabilities, relying exclusively on either one may impose limitations. Self-supervision can reinforce internal errors or preserve existing blind spots, whereas collaborative supervision may introduce unreliable external signals, communication overhead, or excessive dependence on other models. This paper proposes an Adaptive Self-and-Inter Supervision Framework (ASISF) for a general class of Self-and-Inter Models. The framework treats self-supervision and inter-model collaborative supervision as two dynamically selectable learning pathways within a unified model-level architecture. Rather than prescribing a fixed supervision strategy, ASISF evaluates the expected learning benefit, signal reliability, uncertainty, disagreement, computational cost, and resource availability associated with alternative supervision pathways. Based on these assessments, the system can select self-supervision, collaborative supervision, a hybrid strategy, or a temporary fallback strategy. The framework is independent of any specific model architecture, learning algorithm, supervision signal, or application domain. We formally define the Self-and-Inter Model setting, introduce an adaptive supervision policy, formulate a general optimization objective, and present a model-agnostic algorithm. We further establish research propositions concerning learning efficiency, robustness, communication cost, and adaptation under changing conditions. An experimental protocol is proposed to compare adaptive supervision against fixed self-supervision, fixed collaborative supervision, and non-adaptive hybrid learning. The paper contributes a conceptual framework and testable hypotheses rather than claiming experimentally demonstrated improvements. It provides a foundation for investigating how models can autonomously determine when to learn from themselves, when to learn through other models, and when to combine both pathways.

title: Full State-Based CS-QTM: An Architecture for Question Intervention Control in LLM-Based Chatbots
abstract: Questions in large language model (LLM)-based chatbots can elicit information, but unnecessary questions create over-intervention, and omissions create under-intervention. We formulate question timing as a control problem and present Full State-Based CS-QTM. The architecture combines Episode Memory, accumulated question state qt, readinesst, question_scoret, adaptive_thresholdt, Prompt Routing, Hard Reset, Cooldown, and Topic Shift handling. A threshold was selected on a conversation-disjoint development set and frozen before evaluation. Evaluation covered 100 Korean dialogue scenarios and 645 turns, with 180 question-mark-aligned Ask and 465 Not Ask operational references. Qwen Frozen Full obtained F1 = 0.3226 versus 0.2332 for the same-generator Local LLM-only; a shallow sequential classifier trained on development data obtained F1 = 0.6139, revealing surface and sequential regularities in labels. Without retuning, EXAONE Frozen Full and LLM-only obtained F1 = 0.3024 and 0.2865. Controlled comparisons showed that threshold policy and generated-context forcing shifted the over-/under-intervention balance; grouped linguistic-feature effects remained uncertain after multiplicity correction. Internal logs separated policy, visible realization, resets, cooldown, topic shifts, and FP/FN paths. These results permit inspection of the closed-loop control process; they do not establish universal model superiority, optimal timing, or benchmark state-of-the-art.

title: Quantum-Resistant Cryptography for Cloud Security
abstract: The increasing reliance on cloud storage across sectors has made the protection of sensitive data a critical concern especially as advances in quantum computing threaten to break traditional public-key cryptographic systems. This growing vulnerability raises urgent questions about how to secure digital assets in a post-quantum future. To address this challenge, this study aims to design, implement, and evaluate a hybrid encryption framework that combines symmetric encryption for data confidentiality with quantum-resistant public-key algorithms for key management and digital signatures. The objective was to develop a secure and practical solution that can be readily adopted using open-source tools. The system was built in a Linux-based virtual environment using an S3-compatible object storage platform, integrated with quantum-safe cryptographic libraries, and automated through scripting. Performance testing was conducted using files ranging from 100 MB to 1 GB, with metrics such as encryption and decryption time, CPU usage, upload/download latency, and internet throughput analyzed. The results showed that while quantum-safe operations added some overhead, even large files could be securely processed in under two minutes with stable system performance and no data corruption. These findings confirm that hybrid encryption models can be deployed today without specialized hardware, offering a forward-compatible and robust approach to cloud security. This work contributes a tested and reproducible framework for early adoption of quantum-safe cryptography in real-world cloud environments.

title: Adaptive Learning Systems for Children with Special Needs: A Systematic Review
abstract: The growing emphasis on inclusive education and personalised learning underscores the need for effective educational strategies for children with special needs. While inclusive practices hold promise, their success often depends on individualised support. Adaptive learning systems, powered by advancements in AI and multimodal data, offer significant potential to tailor educational content and methods to the unique cognitive, behavioural and emotional profiles of these children. Hence, this systematic review aims to synthesise empirical evidence on the design, effectiveness and implementation of adaptive learning systems for children with special needs. The review was conducted following the PRISMA guidelines. A systematic search of the Scopus database (1 January 2015 – 31 October 2025) identified 50 relevant empirical studies. Data were extracted and analysed using a structured coding form and thematic synthesis, focusing on study characteristics, adaptive technologies, strategies, outcomes and implementation factors. Future development should focus on disability-specific research, stronger evidence, and ethical, collaborative design involving educators, families, and children.

title: What It Is, Not What It Says: Securing Agentic Browsing Interactions with Web Semantics
abstract: AI agents increasingly browse the web on users' behalf, yet they consume webpages as screenshots or text, exposing their LLMs to unvetted third-party content. Browsers enforce semantics under which what an element can do depends on what it is and where it comes from, not on what it says. Agents flatten these semantics, so injected text can persuade the LLM to exercise the user's authority for content that has none. As LLMs remain easy to persuade, the agent's interface to the web must itself ensure the integrity of what the agent reads, interprets, and does. We propose Intact, which runs on an unmodified browser. Intact builds GenTree, a bespoke representation that captures provenance and web semantics. Intact passes the page via GenTree to the LLM one element at a time, so the LLM decides on each element without any other element's text. Its harness executes each step only within the capabilities of the step's element and asks the user before acting on third-party content. On 1,270 real webpages, GenTree attributes 2.3x as many elements to third parties as the browser, which misattributes 58.7% of them to the first party. On 1,091 of these webpages with injected attacks, only 12.8% of attacks get through Intact's planner, each at most as a consent request, against 73.1% for a conventional planner. Isolation disrupts functionality on only 3.7% of tasks, and a parallel schedule could remove most of its added latency.

title: Looking Beyond Visibility: Resolving the Temporal Structure of Continuous-Wave Four-Photon Hong-Ou-Mandel Interference
abstract: Hong-Ou-Mandel interference underpins many photonic quantum information protocols and is commonly characterized by a single visibility parameter. This quantity is typically obtained by averaging over a fixed coincidence window, thereby discarding details of the underlying temporal structure that are critical in continuous-wave processes. Four-photon interference with continuous-wave sources furthermore requires photon pairs with long coherence times, which we generate in microring resonators and measure with ultrafast time-resolved detection. Here, we model and resolve their interference and temporal structure by recording all four photon arrival times and mapping their relative delays onto a three-dimensional coincidence histogram relative to a trigger detection. The resulting structure preserves relative arrival-time correlations that are usually discarded and enables post-processed optimization of coincidence windows to trade off visibility against count rate. This method provides a general benchmark for continuous-wave sources in interference-based quantum network protocols.

title: Crossovers between Time-Bin and Energy-Time Entanglement in Homodyned Resonance Fluorescence
abstract: We theoretically investigate photonic entanglement generated by homodyning resonance fluorescence from a two-level emitter with a phase-locked laser field. Under weak excitation, increasing the relative laser-field amplitude produces crossovers from time-bin to energy--time and back to time-bin entanglement. The intermediate energy--time regime occurs near amplitude matching, where destructive interference suppresses the single-photon component, allowing the two-photon contributions to dominate the coincidence signal. We evaluate the resulting photon statistics and first-order coherence and characterize the entanglement through violations of the CHSH Bell inequality in a Franson interferometer. This scheme provides a route to controlling photonic entanglement through linear optics and coherent interference.

title: CertEx: Exact Visual Retrieval at Scale by Certified Exclusion
abstract: Exact $k$-nearest-neighbor (kNN) search over image descriptors and embeddings underlies visual retrieval, near-duplicate detection, the evaluation of learned representations, and increasingly the memory of LLM agents. However, exhaustive search computes every distance at full precision, whereas approximate indexes return recall below one. We observe that exact search only needs a proof that each excluded vector cannot be a neighbor. Because such a proof only has to be conservative, it can be checked in low precision, much as the retina examines the whole scene at low resolution. We call this principle certified exclusion and realize it in an exact kNN method for GPUs, which we call \certex. Specifically, \certex\ stores a lower-bounding projection of each vector in half precision and folds a rounding certificate into the same tensor-core dot product, so that only the few vectors that the test keeps need exact distances. We prove that \certex\ returns the exact kNN of every query. On sixteen datasets with up to 100M vectors, \certex\ is exact for every query at 7.1$\times$ to 18.0$\times$ the throughput of the fastest cuVS search on one H100 and outperforms quantized and graph indexes whenever every query must be exact.

title: Quantum Scattering Model of Dual-Parallel Mach–Zehnder Electro-Optic Modulators: General Formalism, Impairments, and Applications to Frequency-Bin Photonic Quantum States
abstract: We present a quantum mechanical model of dual parallel Mach Zehnder electro-optic modulators (DPMZMs), derived using the quantum scattering formalism [1,2]. We obtain the complete, unrestricted transformation of single-photon and coherent input states through the DPMZM architecture, including independent radiofrequency drive conditions on each internal modulator, and recover the symmetric push pull operating point as an exact special case. We numerically evaluate the resulting frequency comb structure, quantify the device sensitivity to bias error, modulation-index imbalance, and RF noise, and use the model to design a DP-MZM-based frequency-bin qubit source, reporting its fidelity as a function of these impairments.

title: IIIS: An Inter-Intelligence Intermediary Syntax for Shared Observation Across Perceptions
abstract: How can two intelligences that perceive the world differently share one and the same knowledge structure? We assume the existence of an intelligence whose perception differs from that of humans, and ask what syntactic structure would let such intelligences communicate. We propose that an intermediary syntactic structure — which we call an inter-intelligence intermediary syntax (IIIS) — makes such shared observation possible, and we show that it is constructible. As one implementation, we present EchoScript (ES): a flat, two-column, pipe-separated structure in which the pipe is a mere divider carrying no meaning of its own. The same ES is observed by an artificial intelligence as JSON and by a human as a two-column table — one structure, two perceptions. We conclude that an inter-intelligence intermediary syntax for shared observation across differing perceptions is constructible.

title: An Auditable Binary Evidence-Escalation Protocol for Prompt-Constrained Retrieval-Augmented Question Answering
abstract: Technical-support and engineering knowledge services must decide whether one selected passage is sufficient or additional retrieved evidence should enter the generation prompt. Aggregate accuracy and mean context size conceal whether expansion recovers omitted evidence, adds no value, or harms an otherwise correct answer. We present an auditable binary evidence-escalation protocol for this operational decision. A logistic controller uses 27 pre-generation question and evidence-scoring features to select either one document or a model–task-specific full-candidate action; its outcome-derived development target is configuration-specific, and the resulting policy comparison is conditional on the single development-selected fit rather than an out-of-sample estimate of controller-selection performance. We evaluate deterministic distractor-augmented stress tests derived from SQuAD, WikiQA, and HotpotQA using two open-weight generators and one opaque GPT-compatible API. In the revision-locked GPT/API analysis, the SQuAD-Hard policy had the same observed accuracy as the full-candidate reference (0.9025; paired difference 0.0000, 95% bootstrap CI [−0.0175,0.0175]) while reducing mean prompted documents from 5.00 to 2.74 and reconstructed normalized prompt tokens by 40.8% (95% bootstrap CI [37.3%,44.4%]). No equivalence margin was prespecified. Under the present six-document candidate configuration, WikiQA-Hard provides no practical prompt-evidence benefit: the controller escalated 95.9% of examples and reduced mean prompted documents by only 0.21 of 6 (2.9% token reduction), whereas HotpotQA-Hard incurred an observed accuracy loss of 0.0350. These held-out comparisons quantify test-instance variation conditional on the selected controller; they do not include retraining or controller-selection uncertainty. Paired transition accounting and a bounded case audit distinguish selection, generation, and measurement failures. The protocol provides a design-time audit for prompt-evidence budgets in engineering knowledge and technical-support QA; these benchmark results do not establish production readiness, superiority to adaptive RAG, or latency, energy, or monetary savings.

title: From conversation to green intention: how perceived AI chatbot empathy shapes sustainable travel
abstract: Recent developments in artificial intelligence (AI) have expanded the role of conversational agents in hospitality and travel service encounters. However, it remains unclear how the conversational characteristics of AI become psychologically meaningful and relate to travelers’ sustainable decision-making. Drawing on Cognitive Appraisal Theory (CAT), this study examines the associations between Chatbot Conversational Quality (CCQ) and Green Travel Intention (GTI) through the sequential roles of Perceived Chatbot Empathy (PCE) and Green Travel Motivation (GTM), while considering Eco-Friendly Customer Innovativeness (EFCI) as a boundary condition. Survey data from 400 travelers show that CCQ is associated with PCE, which in turn is associated with stronger GTM and, subsequently, higher GTI. EFCI strengthens the PCE-GTM relationship but does not significantly moderate GTM-GTI, suggesting greater relevance during motivation formation than motivation-to-intention translation. The findings show how conversational AI interactions can acquire socio-emotional meaning in hospitality contexts and highlight customer heterogeneity in sustainability-related decisions.

title: A review of offline training of robotic manipulator control under limited data
abstract: Offline reinforcement learning (RL) has emerged as a promising paradigm for robotic skill acquisition, particularly for manipulation tasks where real-world trial-and-error interaction is costly, time-consuming, or unsafe. In contrast to broad offline RL surveys, this paper presents a focused narrative review centered on robotic manipulation under data-limited conditions, where datasets often suffer from narrow state–action coverage, sparse successful demonstrations, noisy trajectories, and limited behavioral diversity. These constraints exacerbate key challenges in offline RL, including distributional shift, unstable value estimation, weak reward propagation under sparsity, and poor policy generalization. This paper adopts a focused narrative review methodology; it does not claim systematic review status and does not follow a PRISMA protocol, but instead provides a structured, evidence-informed synthesis of representative offline RL methods selected for their methodological significance, benchmark relevance, and applicability to data-limited robotic manipulation conditions. The review analyzes major families of offline RL methods, including conservative value-based approaches, behavior-constrained learning, advantage-weighted methods, uncertainty-aware techniques, model-based offline RL, sequence-modeling approaches, and offline-to-online adaptation strategies. The discussion is grounded in benchmark observations from D4RL and NeoRL, alongside evidence from robotic manipulation systems such as QT-Opt and RoboNet. Comparative analysis suggests that conservative and uncertainty-aware methods typically offer stronger robustness and policy stability under constrained robotic datasets, whereas behavior-constrained and advantage-based approaches remain highly sensitive to dataset quality, behavioral diversity, and reward structure. Model-based and sequence-modeling methods can further improve data efficiency and long-horizon capability, but introduce additional challenges related to model reliability, synthetic rollout fidelity, and sequential data requirements. The paper also discusses practical issues in real-world deployment, including safety constraints, contact instability, sensor noise, and safe online adaptation. Finally, it highlights future research directions such as uncertainty-aware learning, physics-informed world models, foundation models, representation learning, and safe offline-to-online adaptation for robotic manipulation. Overall, this review provides a targeted synthesis of offline RL methods for robotic manipulation under realistic data-scarce conditions, while identifying key limitations, benchmark trends, and open research challenges for next-generation robotic learning systems.

title: Multimodal Filesystem Memory For Long-Horizon Embodied Agents
abstract: Agents operating over long horizons need an effective memory that allows them to reuse their experience throughout long interactions. If the entire history of an interaction is retained, it becomes difficult to find the relevant experience, while compressing it into summaries may result in the loss of visual and spatial details that are required later on. We present MFM, a multimodal filesystem memory architecture that keeps complementary types of agent memory. Episodic memory stores the observations, actions, and outcomes, and spatial memory associates experiences with locations. Semantic and procedural memory build up general knowledge and reusable methods of acting, and working memory holds the current plans. MFM makes use of searchable textual records to connect these different representations to the underlying multimodal episodes. The agents are able to find previous experiences by means of contextual cues and to examine the original observations in order to recover details that are missing from their textual descriptions. Through consolidation, the agents convert experience into higher-level knowledge and procedures while still keeping references to the original episodes. In the case of long-horizon Minecraft and computer-use tasks, MFM leads to improved performance with three base models. With GPT-6-Astra, MFM completes Mine Diamond from Scratch and reaches 16 out of 24 milestones on the Ender Dragon task, as against 12.7 for the best baseline. On CUABench-KiCad it attains a mean reward of 0.440, as compared to 0.400 for the best baseline and 0.267 in the case of no persistent memory.

title: LCT: Losslessly Compressed Tensors with GPU friendly execution for Training
abstract: Lossless tensor compression could reduce memory usage during training, but training requires tensors to be repeatedly re-encoded. We introduce Losslessly Compressed Tensors (LCT), a GPU execution framework designed for this repeated encode-decode regime. LCT exploits the natural redundancy in floating point data to reduce storage for weights, activations and optimizer states. Highly optimized GPU kernels implement Huffman coding with precomputed codebooks for low compression and decompression overhead, essential for training. Our analysis characterizes LCT's storage costs and adaptation to magnitude shifts. LCT achieves a compression ratio of up to $1.455\times$, and is demonstrated in training and finetuning settings. On a 162M-parameter NanoGPT, LCT reduces memory usage by $24.6\%$ for a $7.2\%$ step-time increase. In Qwen3-4B fine-tuning, LCT saves up to $23.8\%$ of peak memory, enabling a $3.5\times$ larger context length in training on the same GPU.

title: Inflak: A Unified Orchestration Architecture for Human-Agent Interaction
abstract: LLM-powered agents increasingly support open-ended activities, yet orchestrating when and how agents interact with humans remains challenging. Existing approaches often provide interaction mechanisms tied to particular tasks or execution patterns, lacking a unified architecture for diverse and evolving interaction needs. We introduce Inflak, a unified four-layer architecture for human-agent interaction orchestration that separates state reconstruction and routing, interaction and execution planning, interaction design, and interface rendering. Its layered design with progressive resolution enables general applicability, runtime flexibility, module composability, and orchestration maintainability. We implement Inflak as agent-native, skill-based plugins within a general-purpose agent framework and evaluate it through a gallery of various application scenarios and interaction paradigms, technical performance testing, and a comparative implementation case study. The evaluations show that Inflak can serve as a general and extensible foundation for orchestrating diverse human-agent interaction flows.

title: From Sketch to Scene: Relightable Garment Reconstruction from Marked Sketches
abstract: Sketching is one of the most natural ways for people to express visual ideas. Unlike the text prompts that most generative systems rely on today, a sketch captures spatial structure and intent directly, including where a designer wants highlights and shadows to appear. Yet current sketch-to-3D pipelines have no input for that intent: they bake the drawn shading into the texture as dark paint, and the light cannot be moved. We propose a system that transforms a rough garment sketch, marked with sparse annotations (a star for a highlight and a moon for a shadow), and a short text prompt describing the texture, into a textured 3D mesh with an explicit directional light, as a scene that can be relit and edited after generation. The two symbols are the most frequent proposals in an elicitation study with art students. From the marked sketch the system predicts the scene's directional light and, separately, a displacement field that bends the surface so that the moon-marked regions fall into shadow under that light, rather than being painted dark in the texture.

title: Zoetrope: A Deadline-Aware Architecture for Continuous Multimodal Perception, Reasoning, and Authorized Action
abstract: A live visual assistant must do more than describe successive images: it must maintain a coherent account of an evolving situation, allocate reasoning effort before relevant opportunities expire, and distinguish an authorized action from a plausible but outdated suggestion. We propose Zoetrope, a model-agnostic architecture for continuous multimodal perception, asynchronous reasoning, and bounded intervention. Its starting configuration samples every other frame of a video stream. Rather than equating this sampling frequency with the frequency or latency of complete reasoning, Zoetrope separates observation ingestion, temporal state maintenance, reasoning admission, and action execution. A versioned evidence store connects claims to timestamped observations; a deadline-aware scheduler allocates deeper inference; and an independent execution gate revalidates permissions and action-critical evidence before an intervention. The design supports both responsive questions and standing requests that require proactive notice or action, while perception continues during response generation. We formalize the distinction between throughput and freshness, specify bounded-memory and overload behavior, and develop a causal evaluation protocol that measures deadline-conditioned correctness, stale-state errors, interruption burden, and resource use. The central hypothesis is that explicit evidence validity and selective reasoning improve useful real-time performance over isolated frame analysis and asynchronous systems without freshness checks. This manuscript presents an architecture, analytical constraints, and an experimental plan; it reports no implementation measurements or benchmark results.

title: BUXORO HUDUDI O'ZBEK SHEVALARI VARIANTLARINI AVTOMATIK ANIQLASH USULLARI
abstract: Annotatsiya: Ushbu tezisda Buxoro hududi o‘zbek shevalarining fonetik, leksik va morfologik xususiyatlarini kompyuter lingvistikasi usullari yordamida avtomatik aniqlash va tasniflash masalalari yoritilgan. Shuningdek, shevalarga xos til birliklarini aniqlash, ularni standart o‘zbek tili birliklaridan farqlash hamda avtomatik tasniflash imkoniyatlari tahlil qilinadi. Buxoro shevalarining o‘ziga xos xususiyatlarini raqamli ma’lumotlar asosida qayta ishlash va lingvistik modellar yordamida tasniflash usullari ko‘rib chiqiladi. Olingan natijalar o‘zbek shevalarini kompyuter yordamida tadqiq etish, elektron lingvistik resurslar yaratish va shevalarning raqamli korpusini shakllantirish uchun muhim ahamiyat kasb etadi. Kalit so’zlar: kompyuter lingvistikasi, NLP, buxoro shevasi, dialektalogiya, avtomatik aniqlash, korpus lingvistikasi. Аннотация: В данной тезисной работе рассматриваются вопросы автоматического выявления и классификации фонетических, лексических и морфологических особенностей узбекских говоров Бухарского региона с использованием методов компьютерной лингвистики. Также анализируются возможности выявления языковых единиц, характерных для диалектов, их разграничения от единиц стандартного узбекского языка и автоматической классификации. Рассматриваются методы обработки специфических особенностей бухарских говоров на основе цифровых данных и их классификации с использованием лингвистических моделей. Полученные результаты имеют важное значение для компьютерного исследования узбекских диалектов, создания электронных лингвистических ресурсов и формирования цифрового корпуса узбекских говоров. Ключевые слова: компьютерная лингвистика, NLP, бухарский говор, диалектология, автоматическое выявление, корпусная лингвистика. Abstract: This thesis examines the automatic identification and classification of the phonetic, lexical, and morphological features of Uzbek dialects in the Bukhara region using computational linguistics methods. It also analyzes the possibilities of identifying dialect-specific linguistic units, distinguishing them from standard Uzbek language units, and classifying them automatically. The study considers methods for processing the distinctive features of Bukhara dialects based on digital data and classifying them using linguistic models. The results obtained are of significant importance for computer-assisted research on Uzbek dialects, the development of electronic linguistic resources, and the compilation of a digital corpus of Uzbek dialects. Keywords: computational linguistics, NLP, Bukhara dialect, dialectology, automatic identification, corpus linguistics.

title: COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS OF TRADITIONAL ENDOSCOPY AND AI BASED SYSTEMS
abstract: Reliable gastric ulcer detection depends on both systematic endoscopic inspection and the quality of the recorded images. Motion blur, specular reflections, bubbles and mucosal debris can obscure lesion margins and compromise automated analysis. This paper compares conventional endoscopic evaluation with artificial intelligence assisted image interpretation through a focused literature based analysis and a proposed evaluation framework. It examines artifact mechanisms, preprocessing options, model selection and clinical oversight. The central conclusion is that automated detection should be coupled with image quality assessment and transparent reporting. Enhancement cannot recover tissue information that was never captured, and performance on selected clean images cannot establish clinical reliability. A patient separated evaluation, artifact stratification and external validation are therefore necessary before claims of diagnostic superiority can be made. No new clinical experiment or validated accuracy estimate is reported in this paper.

title: Building Customer Trust Through Responsible AI
abstract: Artificial intelligence now sits at the heart of digital marketing. Firms rely on it for everything from personalized product recommendations and automated customer conversations to predictive analytics, dynamic pricing, and real-time campaign adjustments. Yet these same capabilities carry real risks. Data is collected in ways customers may not expect. Algorithms can reflect hidden biases. Automated messages can veer into manipulation. And when customers sense any of this, trust is the first thing to go .Drawing on Trust Theory, Privacy Calculus Theory, Stakeholder Theory, Signaling Theory, and the Resource-Based View, the chapter sets out a framework that connects responsible AI practices to customer trust, marketing outcomes, and financial outcomes. The core argument is simple but important: responsible AI is not mainly a technical or compliance matter. It is a cross-functional marketing and financial capability that allows firms to build lasting customer relationships in markets where data is everywhere and trust is harder to earn than ever.

title: Feature-token clinical transformer for 24-h landmark mortality risk stratification in critically ill patients with heart failure: development and multicenter external validation
abstract: Background The first 24 h after ICU admission in critically ill patients with heart failure yield heterogeneous EHR evidence across vital signs, laboratory tests, treatments, organ support, and nurse-charted monitoring. Conventional scores and flat-vector ML models may not preserve individual variable identity or context. Methods We developed FTCT, encoding each predictor recorded during the first 24 h after ICU admission as a clinically tagged token (value, missingness, identity, group). MIMIC-IV (2008–2019) served for development, validation, and internal testing; eICU-CRD (2014–2015) served for external validation. Included were adults with heart failure, a complete 24-h ICU observation window, and known discharge status. The endpoint was in-hospital all-cause death. Results MIMIC-IV included 11,156 stays and 1,484 deaths, partitioned into training ( n = 7,809), validation ( n = 1,673), and internal test ( n = 1,674) sets. eICU-CRD included 9,837 stays and 1,319 deaths. FTCT achieved an AUROC of 0.849 (95% CI, 0.835–0.863) internally and 0.804 (0.788–0.820) externally. Patient-paired AUROC differences vs. XGBoost were 0.027 (0.011–0.043) internally and 0.032 (0.014–0.050) externally. A matched FT-Transformer-style baseline achieved an external AUROC of 0.781 (0.760–0.801). In eICU-CRD, FTCT achieved an AUPRC of 0.296 (0.278–0.314), Brier score of 0.091 (0.085–0.097), and expected calibration error of 0.036 (0.030–0.042). In a post hoc cohort-specific descriptive operating analysis targeting approximately 85% specificity, external sensitivity was 0.662 (0.636–0.687), positive predictive value 0.406 (0.385–0.427), negative predictive value 0.942 (0.937–0.947), and F1 score 0.503. Removing feature-token encoding produced the largest ablation loss in external AUROC (−0.031). Conclusions FTCT combines established feature-token Transformer modeling with clinical-group embeddings, explicit missingness representation, and group-aware pooling for 24-h landmark mortality risk stratification from structured EHR data recorded during the first 24 h after ICU admission. Its external validation and ablation results support prospective investigation, but do not yet demonstrate clinical utility, workflow integration, admission-time applicability, or autonomous use.

title: "LoRa RFFI Cross-Domain Dataset for Secure Device Authentication"
abstract: "This dataset contains raw Software Defined Radio baseband recordings and their processed spectrogram tensor counterparts for benchmarking Radio-Frequency Fingerprinting Identification (RFFI) models that perform physical-layer device authentication. Cross-domain fingerprint generalization and open-set rogue hardware rejection capacities are the main directions of research under consideration.The environment-pooled method is used for training the deep learning models in order to achieve invariance to the measurement conditions. The baseband recordings are not partitioned according to the measurement environment during training. Instead, the data was pooled from four distinct physical domains during the first step of model training. As a result, the deep learning models are forced to learn how to cancel out the characteristics of the communication channel and focus on the unique hardware distortions present in every transmitter.The dataset is further split into a three-stage pipeline for research purposes. The continuous baseband recordings, spectrogram tensors that have been regularized to standard computer vision sizes, and packets with regularized Zero-Forcing channel equalization can all be used as inputs. The latter, which is the training pool, contains hardware fingerprints with carrier frequency offset, phase noise, IQ imbalance software-induced distortions to generalize over transceivers. The open-set authentication is enabled by hold-out fingerprints of the authorized node and attack vectors in an entirely separate physical transceiver."

title: Experimental Data for Implementation-Aware Real-Time Benchmark of Incremental PI and Mamdani Fuzzy Logic Speed Control for a Brushed DC Motor
abstract: This dataset contains the experimental data supporting the manuscript entitled Implementation-Aware Real-Time Benchmark of Incremental PI and Mamdani Fuzzy Logic Speed Control for a Brushed DC Motor. The experiments compare an incremental proportional–integral controller and a fixed-rule Mamdani Type-1 fuzzy logic controller implemented on the same Texas Instruments TMS320F2812 DSP platform. Both controllers were evaluated using identical encoder feedback, QEP-based speed estimation, a 1 ms sampling period, PWM actuation, voltage-command limitation, supply conditions, measured channels, and KPI-extraction procedures. The dataset covers nominally no-load step-response experiments at reference speeds of 955 rpm and 6685 rpm. The recorded quantities include reference speed, measured motor speed, voltage-equivalent command monitor, and armature current. The associated performance indicators include 10–90% rise time, percentage overshoot, ±1% settling time, transient peak armature current, and steady-state armature current. The files are organized by controller and operating point. A README file describes the file structure, variable names, units, controller parameters, and the procedure used to reproduce the reported performance indicators and figures.

title: AlphaBet: Reinforcement Learning for LLM Event Forecasting Agents
abstract: Forecasting an unresolved event requires finding relevant evidence and deciding how strongly it supports each outcome. Yet outcome-based training of Large Language Model (LLM) forecasters often begins with preassembled evidence at a single prediction date, leaving evidence acquisition outside the learning loop. We introduce AlphaBet, an agentic reinforcement learning (RL) framework that trains a single LLM policy to search, reason, and report probabilities across multiple pre-resolution dates. Each dated forecast is scored by a proper scoring rule against the eventual outcome, allowing one resolved event to supervise decisions under different information states. We decompose forecasting regret into an evidence-acquisition gap and a probability-reporting gap, and show that Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO)'s standard-deviation normalization can distort the reporting target under multi-class proper scores. On GLM-4.5-Air, AlphaBet reduces the Brier score from 0.731 to 0.626 on Forecast-Dojo and from 0.612 to 0.528 on FutureX. Controlled ablations attribute these gains to multi-date training and show that they come from improvements in both information acquisition and probability reporting. Our empirical results validate that GRPO's std normalization degrades proper-scoring-rule performance while leaving top-outcome accuracy largely unchanged.

title: Accurate gap control of 3D-integrated superconducting quantum circuits using asymmetric indium architecture and multi-angle flip-chip bonding
abstract: Flip-chip 3D integration is a key enabling technology for overcoming the routing and layout constraints of planar superconducting quantum processors, but it requires accurate and uniform control of the inter-chip spacing while preserving qubit coherence. In conventional processes, thick indium bumps are deposited symmetrically on both chips, while dedicated spacers are introduced to limit the residual tilt. Here, we present a flip-chip bonding process based on an asymmetric indium architecture, combining $20\,μ\mathrm{m}$ thick indium bumps on the control chip with $200\,\mathrm{nm}$ thin indium pads on the qubit chip. Using electrical and microwave measurements, we demonstrate low resistance and low loss indium interconnects, and show that transmon qubits integrated with this process reach relaxation and coherence times of $T_1=(159\pm14)\,μ\mathrm{s}$ and $T_{\mathrm{2,echo}}=(294\pm42)\,μ\mathrm{s}$, respectively, comparable to planar devices. Combined with a multi angle compression procedure that suppresses systematic tilt, this approach reduces the average post bonding tilt to $(20\pm12)\,μ\mathrm{rad}$. These results establish an asymmetric indium architecture combined with multi angle compression as a robust, coherence preserving route toward 3D integrated superconducting quantum processors.

title: CoViG: Coarsened Vision GNN for Image Classification
abstract: Although Graph Neural Networks are widely used in various domains, they remained mostly unexplored in computer vision. Convolutional Neural Networks and Vision Transformers were leading the field, until the quite recent introduction of Vision Graphs (ViG) that treat images as a set of nodes and apply graph convolution on their k-NN graphs. ViGs show impressive accuracy on image classification but their computational cost remains relatively high. Inspired by optimization methods for GNNs, we present CoViG, a novel approach combining graph coarsening and ViGs. Our method introduces an additional MinCUT pooling step within the Grapher component of intermediate ViG blocks. evidence.abstract: Although Graph Neural Networks are widely used in various domains, they remained mostly unexplored in computer vision. Convolutional Neural Networks and Vision Transformers were leading the field, until the quite recent introduction of Vision Graphs (ViG) that treat images as a set of nodes and apply graph convolution on their k-NN graphs. ViGs show impressive accuracy on image classification but their computational cost remains relatively high. Inspired by optimization methods for GNNs, we present CoViG, a novel approach combining graph coarsening and ViGs. Our method introduces an additional MinCUT pooling step within the Grapher component of intermediate ViG blocks. title: Evidence Field for Histopathology: Cross-Centre Evaluation and Replayable Spatial Decisions
abstract: Histopathology classifiers must transfer across acquisition sites while exposing evidence that can be checked independently. Evidence Field couples learned image measurements and spatial classification with a native covering-program record. We evaluate this architecture on all 455,954 released CAMELYON17-WILDS patches, using patient-separated source partitions and two held-out hospital centres. Eighteen from-scratch fits compare four Evidence Field objectives with residual convolutional and compact vision-transformer classifiers. Checkpoints, temperatures and review thresholds are selected using source validation. The source-selected paired-cross-entropy ensemble achieves areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.9356 and 0.9453, with accuracies of 84.46% and 86.77% at the two held-out centres. Corresponding convolutional values are 0.7352 and 0.7656, and transformer values are 0.8502 and 0.7924. Evidence Field has 10,550 trainable parameters per member and additionally returns selected covers, signed region and interaction terms, contextual dependencies and independently reconstructible predictions. Patient-cluster intervals, calibration, source-fixed review policies and recorded training resources characterize the results. A 340-image, three-member audit reconstructs probability mixtures and 6,120 class programs under three rigid views. The evaluation supports cross-centre discrimination and reproducible computation for these implemented models; unequal family tuning, previously examined public targets and limited patient groups constrain broader interpretation.

title: The Co-Evolution of Quantum Physics and Finance
abstract: Quantum physics and finance are often connected through mathematical analogy or promises of computational acceleration. This article develops an alternative account of asymmetric co-evolution. A selective conceptual synthesis distinguishes shared mathematical ancestry, explicit transfer, and reciprocal innovation across uncertainty, valuation, measurement, computation, and monetary security. Quantum theory supplies representational and computational possibilities; financial problems impose constraints that can redirect quantum information research. Documented feedback is strongest in algorithm design and cryptographic tasks. This article proposes testable research directions concerning investor judgment, financial validation, decision-relevant computational advantage, market adoption, and quantum money. Progress requires reciprocal discipline: quantum methods must satisfy financial restrictions, while finance must incorporate the physical and computational conditions governing information.

title: The Dark Side of Generative AI in Marketing: AI-Generated False and Misleading Advertising and Its Consumer Consequences
abstract: Abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is transforming advertising by enabling marketers to create persuasive text, images, and other promotional content rapidly and at lower cost. At the same time, the ability of generative systems to produce highly realistic content creates concerns about deception, misinformation, transparency, and the credibility of consumer-facing information. The present study examines the consumer consequences of AI-generated false and misleading advertising, with particular emphasis on hallucinated product claims. The study focuses on whether AI-generated hallucinated product claims influence perceived deception, AI skepticism, and perceived information reliability, and whether these consumer responses subsequently shape purchase intention. Drawing on the stimulus-organism-response (S-O-R) framework, the study conceptualizes hallucinated product claims as the stimulus, the three consumer evaluations as the organism, and purchase intention as the response. A quantitative, cross-sectional, deductive research design was adopted. Data were collected from 320 business-school students and faculty members through a structured questionnaire using a five-point Likert scale, and the model was assessed using SmartPLS. The reported measurement results show Cronbach's alpha values above 0.70, composite reliability above the stated threshold, and average variance extracted above 0.50 for all constructs, indicating acceptable reliability and convergent validity. The reported discriminant-validity matrix also supports construct distinctiveness. The structural model reports a VIF range of 1.47-2.24 and an R² of 0.421 for purchase intention. Four of the six hypotheses are supported. AI-generated hallucinated product claims significantly increase perceived deception and significantly reduce perceived information reliability. Perceived deception significantly reduces purchase intention, while perceived information reliability significantly increases purchase intention. The paths from hallucinated product claims to AI skepticism and from AI skepticism to purchase intention are not statistically significant. The findings indicate that message-level judgments of deception and information reliability are more consequential for purchase intention in the reported model than generalized skepticism toward AI. The study extends the S-O-R perspective to the dark side of GenAI in advertising and highlights the importance of factual verification, transparency, human oversight, disclosure, and consumer AI literacy. Keywords: Generative artificial intelligence; AI hallucinations; misleading advertising; perceived deception; AI skepticism; perceived information reliability; purchase intention; stimulus-organism-response theory.

title: Propuestas novedosas para incrementar y depurar el repertorio dramático de Luis Vélez de Guevara
abstract: El repertorio dramático de Luis Vélez de Guevara nos ha llegado casi en su totalidad tras las correspondientes adaptaciones escénicas e impresas y sin control de la transmisión por parte del poeta. A través de métodos estilométricos ofrecemos propuestas de inclusión y exclusión de obras teatrales al corpus velecista. Se ofrece información sobre 58 piezas que nos han llegado con atribuciones a distintos autores, entre los que figura Luis Vélez, y en las que la estilometría ha detectado su huella, o su ausencia, cuando las fuentes primarias no generaban dudas. Lo más interesante son las 15 atribuciones, muy seguras desde la estilometría, que se relacionan con el dramaturgo, algunas ya señaladas con anterioridad por otros métodos y pistas, lo cual da mucha solidez a lo que aquí se propone. También son relevantes las 29 obras que son rechazadas por esta técnica. Con estas sumas y restas finales, Luis Vélez sigue siendo uno de los dramaturgos con mayor número de obras dramáticas conservadas, en torno al centenar, solo superado por Lope y Calderón.

title: Radial–Angular Feature Shaping with an eXtra-Node and Prototype-Based Cosine Similarity Under Adversarial Perturbations
abstract: Adversarial perturbations can alter neural-network predictions, motivating closer analysis of the geometry of learned feature representations. For a given local displacement in feature space, small-norm feature vectors can undergo larger first-order directional changes than larger-norm vectors. This study examines this geometric effect in a two-dimensional (2D) bottleneck and proposes a composite objective that regulates feature radius and class-aligned direction. A norm-dependent auxiliary eXtra-node contributes a direct outward feature-gradient component for nonzero features near the origin, whereas a prototype-based cosine similarity (PCS) term aligns features with normalized classifier-weight directions. An exact comparison with semantic cross-entropy further shows that auxiliary softmax normalization introduces an additional semantic-normalization coupling term with generally mixed radial and tangential components. Experiments on a 10-class subset of ImageNet with six matched CNN and Transformer backbones show that the proposed objective increases both the mean feature radius and the mean similarity to the ground-truth class prototype. Under the FGSM, PGD, FDA, UAP, and DeepFool settings used in the experiments, post-attack accuracy is higher in 26 of 30 backbone–procedure comparisons, while mean clean accuracy changes from 98.69% to 98.15%. These results show that the eXtra-node–PCS objective reshapes the 2D representation in the intended radial and angular directions and support further investigation in standard high-dimensional feature spaces and under adaptive attack evaluation.

title: LWE-Based Threshold Key Management with Dynamic Enrollment and Share Refresh
abstract: We present a trusted-dealer Learning with Errors (LWE)-based threshold key-management framework that separates the public-key layer from threshold-share maintenance. The coordinator generates one LWE public key PK=(A,b),b=As+e(modq) and distributes the same secret vector through coordinate-wise Shamir (t,n) sharing. Dynamic membership is restricted to enrollment: a new participant obtains an evaluation of the existing sharing polynomial, so enrollment does not rotate the secret or change the LWE key pair. Share refresh uses participant-generated degree-(t−1) vector polynomials with zero constant term. Their evaluations are exchanged over authenticated private channels and added locally, preserving the same secret without interpolation or accumulation of LWE error. This paper formalizes exact threshold recovery, single-epoch share privacy, and cross-epoch share-snapshot privacy under a restricted post-refresh observation model with hidden refresh state and effective erasure. It also introduces an explicit epoch-consistency rule so that recovery never mixes shares from different refresh epochs and derives communication and computation costs separately for setup, enrollment, refresh, and recovery. Hash-based commitments and authenticated private channels are treated as integrity and delivery mechanisms rather than as substitutes for maliciously secure verifiable secret sharing (VSS). The post-quantum claim is conditional on concrete validation of the selected LWE parameter tuple. Dealerless distributed key generation (DKG), coordinator-compromise proactive security, participant departure, threshold changes, and a complete quantum random oracle model (QROM) reduction remain outside the present security claims.

title: Exploring The Empirical Privacy Landscape of Synthetic Data
abstract: Methods for training language models on sensitive data differ in how they balance capability gains against the risk of leaking private information. In this paper, we present a controlled comparison of data-level and training-level interventions for navigating the capability-privacy tradeoff on synthetic medical records with canaries to probe for leakage. Direct finetuning performs best on capability metrics but leads to the most privacy leakage, while DP-SGD reduces leakage at substantial cost to capabilities. Generating synthetic data from these records offers a more favorable balance, particularly when guided by a uniqueness-aware instruction to replace private details. Relative to naive paraphrasing, privacy-aware rewriting improves privacy protection across a variety of different rewriting models. We also find that more capable rewriting models generally reduce the risks of downstream privacy leakage, although held-out fit does not improve monotonically and increased test-time compute yields inconsistent gains. Overall, these results highlight privacy-aware rewriting as a promising direction for achieving a more favorable trade-off between capabilities and empirical privacy compared to other training-level methods, and our evaluation framework supports comparisons of future models and methods.

title: Motion- and Gravity-Aware Feedforward 3D Reconstruction
abstract: Feed-forward transformer models have recently achieved strong performance in multi-view 3D reconstruction, but they still rely primarily on appearance-based attention and often struggle in dynamic scenes with weak geometric cues. In this work, we introduce a motion- and gravity-aware framework under the Learning Using Privileged Information (LUPI) paradigm. During training, residual optical flow and gravity direction are provided as privileged signals to guide geometric representation learning; during inference, the model uses standard visual inputs only. We integrate these priors into transformer backbones with lightweight architectural changes, preserving feed-forward efficiency. Experiments on standard benchmarks show consistent gains in reconstruction accuracy and robustness, especially in scenes with dynamic objects, ambiguous structure, and challenging camera motion. Our analysis further shows that the optimal injection stage is backbone-dependent: middle-layer integration is generally preferable for VGGT, while late-stage integration is more effective for π3. These results suggest that LUPI offers a practical way to inject motion and physical priors into feed-forward 3D reconstruction without increasing test-time complexity.

title: Quantum control of solid state qubits via Reinforcement Learning
abstract: The use of reinforcement learning (RL) in the design of quantum control strategies for pulse level control of NISQ era quantum devices is attracting growing interest. Model-free RL, not requiring preexisting knowledge of the physical system, acts as a black-box optimization tool well suited for noisy devices. In this work, we provide a simulation-based analysis of the performance of model-free RL for state preparation and qubit gate design in a challenging setup: indirect control of NV nuclear spins in a spin-bath. In particular, the spin-bath is modeled via the generalized cluster correlation expansion accounting for magnetic impurities and intra-bath interactions. We analyze the performance of the RL agents by performing simulations with minimally observable environments and noisy, sparse rewards as introduced in (Phys. Rev. X 12, 011059), and compare them to other state-of-the-art black-box optimization tools.

title: Seeing Both the Forest and the Trees: Reusing Holistic 3D Priors for Part-Decomposed Generation
abstract: Generating 3D assets with explicit parts requires two properties at once: geometric detail inside each part and structural coherence across the whole object. Recent image-conditioned 3D generation models adopt a structured 3D representation that anchors tokens to explicit spatial positions, capturing both properties, but their output remains a single fused mesh. We ask how a part-decomposed generation model can inherit both properties of these holistic priors, and answer with STRUCTPARTS, a framework whose core technical contribution is a dual-frame coordinate interleaving mechanism: each shape latent is interpreted under both a part-local and an object-global reference frame, and processed through a global-local inter-leaved transformer that simultaneously reuses the prior's geometric detail at the part scale and its structural coherence at the whole-object scale. As its structural input, STRUCTPARTS uses a segmented mesh scaffold, a coarse mesh paired with a face-level segmentation mask kept entirely within the prior's native 3D representation. With only lightweight finetuning, both intra-part detail and inter-part coherence emerge from the same pretrained weights. On PartObjaverse-Tiny, STRUCTPARTS matches or surpasses prior part-decomposed models at a fraction of their training cost, while naturally supporting part-mesh refinement and part-level editing.

title: Hierarchical universal open structure dataset for atomistic modeling
abstract: Atomic-scale simulations have been transformed by machine-learning models that predict the properties of atomistic structures with the accuracy of quantum calculations, but at a small fraction of the cost. These models have increased dramatically in generality, thanks to the availability of synthetic datasets of ever-increasing size and scope. The proliferation of datasets, with properties often computed using different levels of electronic-structure approximation, is problematic, as there is often overlap between different datasets, and strong correlations between structures obtained with short molecular dynamics trajectories or geometry optimization. To address these problems, we introduce a protocol to stratify a dataset into a hierarchy of nested subsets, subsampling from the coarsest to the finest resolution based on an "ecumetric" built to reflect the latent space representation of several popular universal machine-learning interatomic potentials. We then use this approach to combine most of the open structural datasets currently available, consolidating them into MAD-COSMO, a well-organized collection of almost 1.7 billion structures, whose 2^{24} most diverse members form the MAD-CORE stratified coreset, which can be easily used for all sorts of tasks, from exploratory experiments to the training of foundation models at scale. We envision that this collection will guide and help coordinate future efforts, focusing them on the most relevant and/or undersampled regions of chemical and structural space, and that it will be further extended to incorporate the outcomes of the collective work of this community.

title: Uncertainty Quantification in Pairwise Difference Learning for Classification
abstract: Instead of learning a mapping from instances to outcomes in the standard way, the key idea of pairwise difference learning (PDL) is to learn a function that takes two instances as input and predicts the difference between the respective outcomes. Given a function of this kind, predictions for a query instance are derived from every training example and then averaged. We propose a version of PDL for the task of classification and propose a suitable meta-learning technique for this purpose. Moreover, we address the problem of uncertainty quantification, i.e., of representing and quantifying the uncertainty of a PDL classifier's predictions in a faithful manner. Building on recent work on the decomposition of total uncertainty into aleatoric and epistemic components, we propose different ways of extending corresponding measures to the setting of PDL, depending on how and to what extent uncertainty is represented by the underlying base learner. In large-scale empirical studies, we analyze both the predictive accuracy and the uncertainty awareness of our PDL classifier.

Moreover, we address the problem of uncertainty quantification, i.e., of representing and quantifying the uncertainty of a PDL classifier's predictions in a faithful manner. Building on recent work on the decomposition of total uncertainty into aleatoric and epistemic components, we propose different ways of extending corresponding measures to the setting of PDL, depending on how and to what extent uncertainty is represented by the underlying base learner. In large-scale empirical studies, we analyze both the predictive accuracy and the uncertainty awareness of our PDL classifier.

title: SIEVE: Overcoming Topological Obstruction in Equivariant Self-Supervised Learning
abstract: We identify a theoretical incompatibility between 3D point cloud masked autoencoding and SE(3)-equivariant networks. We prove that standard masking triggers a topological collapse, effectively forcing the model to hallucinate orientation without a reference frame. To resolve this, we introduce SIEVE (Scalar Invariant Extraction Via Equivariance), an SE(3)-equivariant self-supervised framework that compresses point cloud geometry into invariant scalar embeddings. At its core is the spherical projection mask, which preserves global pose while obfuscating local semantics, sidestepping the obstruction by construction. Experiments confirm that SIEVE circumvents the predicted collapse where constant and noise masks fail. On downstream point cloud tasks, the resulting embeddings improve over coordinate-based baselines and hand-crafted geometric descriptors, with the largest gains on generalization to unseen shape categories.

title: Solving the Capacitated Vehicle Routing Problem Using the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm: A Benchmark Against Classical Guided Local Search
abstract: The Capacitated Vehicle Routing Problem (CVRP) is a combinatorial optimization problem that can be formulated as a Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) problem, making it a potential application for near-term quantum optimization. This paper benchmarks the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA, p = 2) against Google OR-Tools Guided Local Search on a seeded instance with three customers and two vehicles. The study examines the QUBO formulation, energy spectrum, optimization behavior, penalty weights, Hamiltonian scaling, and circuit depths. The experiments show that the tested QAOA configurations do not reliably concentrate probability on optimal solutions. The classical solver identifies the optimal solution for the selected instance. The study provides a reproducible baseline and discusses limitations and future research directions. The findings are limited to the tested instance, formulation, and optimization configurations.

title: Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG): An Adaptive Framework for Evidence-Grounded Question Answering
abstract: This paper presents a proposed Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) framework for adaptive, evidence-grounded question answering using large language models (LLMs). Unlike conventional single-pass RAG systems, the proposed framework incorporates query planning, retrieval, tool selection, evidence evaluation, answer generation, and self-reflection. The framework uses a bounded feedback loop to improve evidence retrieval when the initial results are insufficient or conflicting. It aims to produce answers supported by relevant source citations while communicating uncertainty when reliable evidence is unavailable. The paper discusses the system architecture, workflow, algorithmic control logic, evaluation methodology, security, privacy, and governance considerations. It also proposes evaluation metrics for answer quality, retrieval effectiveness, factual grounding, latency, computational cost, and component-level ablation studies. Potential applications include research assistance, document question answering, enterprise knowledge management, customer support, and data analysis. This work presents a conceptual framework and proposed evaluation plan. Implementation, benchmark experiments, and measured performance improvements are not reported. Keywords: Agentic RAG, Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Large Language Models, AI Agents, Evidence-Grounded Question Answering, Adaptive Retrieval, Self-Reflection.

title: Adaptive Learning and Collaborative Adaptive Learning Between World Self-Models and World Mutual-Models: A Dynamic Switching Framework
abstract: World models provide internal representations of environmental dynamics that support prediction, simulation, planning, and decision-making. However, learning within a world model and learning through interactions among multiple world models are often treated as separate design choices. Independent adaptation can preserve model-specific knowledge and reduce communication overhead, whereas collaborative adaptation can facilitate knowledge transfer, error correction, and the identification of shared environmental regularities. Neither mode is universally optimal across all tasks, environments, and stages of learning. This paper proposes a conceptual framework for adaptive learning and collaborative adaptive learning between World Self-Models and World Mutual-Models. The framework distinguishes autonomous model adaptation from inter-model collaborative adaptation and introduces a dynamic switching mechanism that selects between these modes according to predictive uncertainty, model disagreement, learning progress, environmental change, expected collaboration benefit, and coordination cost. Rather than requiring continuous collaboration or permanent isolation, the framework treats learning mode selection as a sequential decision problem. A world model can independently update its internal dynamics, selectively request information from other world models, incorporate externally obtained evidence, or return to autonomous learning when collaboration is unnecessary or counterproductive. The proposed architecture includes model-specific state representations, predictive dynamics, uncertainty estimation, collaborative information exchange, adaptive mode selection, and feedback-based evaluation. A formal objective is developed to balance predictive performance, adaptation speed, robustness, knowledge diversity, and computational efficiency. The paper also proposes implementation procedures, research hypotheses, comparative baselines, evaluation metrics, and ablation studies. The framework is intended for model-based reinforcement learning, embodied agents, robotic systems, and other environments in which multiple predictive world models learn related or interacting dynamics. It does not require large language models as its fundamental computational substrate. The proposed framework is a research design rather than an empirically validated algorithm; its effectiveness and novelty relative to existing adaptive multi-agent world-model methods require systematic experimental investigation.

title: ЦИФРОВОЙ ТЕКСТ-АНАЛИЗ ЭЛЕКТРОННЫХ АМБУЛАТОРНЫХ ЗАПИСЕЙ В КЛИНИКО-ЭПИДЕМИОЛОГИЧЕСКОЙ ХАРАКТЕРИСТИКЕ СИНДРОМА КОНСКОГО ХВОСТА: ВОЗМОЖНОСТИ И ОГРАНИЧЕНИЯ ЦИФРОВОЙ МЕДИЦИНЫ
abstract: В работе на примере ретроспективного анализа синдрома конского хвоста (СКХ) продемонстрирован потенциал цифровых методов текст-майнинга неструктурированных электронных амбулаторных записей для быстрой клинико-эпидемиологической характеристики редкой неврологической патологии. Из массива 3054 визитов неврологической клиники методом ключевого поиска и дедупликации сформирована когорта из 323 уникальных пациентов с диагнозом «синдром конского хвоста» (10,6% от всех визитов). Показано преобладание мужчин трудоспособного возраста, среднетяжёлого течения с нарушением функции тазовых органов и вертеброгенной коморбидности; выявлена нетипичная для клиники практика почти повсеместной атрибуции синдрома герпесвирусной/цитомегаловирусной этиологии, что обсуждается в свете современных данных о синдроме Эльсберга. Обоснована перспективность интеграции правило-ориентированного и ИИ/NLP-ассистированного анализа медицинских записей, телемедицинского мониторинга тазовых функций и биомаркер-ориентированной индивидуализированной диагностики в рамках концепции цифровой медицины.

title: Optimizing the Privacy Accuracy Trade-off in Data Stream Mining Using Random Cycle Cumulative Noise Addition
abstract: Data stream mining has become increasingly important as a result of the continuous generation of data in real world applications including healthcare monitoring, sensor networks, transportation systems and online services. While stream classification techniques provide strong predictive performance, publishing or processing such streams raises serious privacy concerns. Perturbation based privacy preserving data stream mining (PPDSM) methods address this issue by adding noise to the data before it is analyzed. Cumulative noise addition accumulates noise across a fixed-size cycle of records give a favourable privacy–accuracy trade-off compared with independent noise addition. However, a fixed cycle size introduces a predictable and periodic structure in the perturbation process. This paper proposes Random-Cycle Cumulative Noise Addition (RC-CNA), a perturbation mechanism that adds noise to random cycle sizes instead of fix-cycle size. RC-CNA is evaluated against the fixedcycle model. The proposed method raises classification accuracy, lowers privacy breach probability, and achieves the overall Privacy–Accuracy trade-off. Proposed method indicates that randomizing the cycle size, combined with the modulation, is a practical improvement that simultaneously strengthens privacy protection and improves classification utility.
